question: A car travels from P to Q with a speed of 45 km/h and from Q to R with a speed of 65 km/h. If the distance from P to Q is 60 km and the distance from Q to R is 100 km, then what is the average speed of the car during the whole journey (corrected to two decimal places)?
solution:
**Given:**

Distance(P-Q) = 60km

Distance(Q-R) = 100km

Speed(P-Q) =45km/h

Speed(Q-R) = 65km/h

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance/Time 

Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time taken

**Solution:**

Total distance = 60 + 100 = 160

Time from P to Q = 60/45 = 1.33 hours

Time from Q to R = 100/65 = 1.538 hours

Total time = 1.33 + 1.538 = 2.868 hours

**Average speed = 160/2.868 = 55.79km/h**
